body:
Q6 FOLLOW-UP — the absence of CI changes the evidence class; it does not make all current documentation impossible.

Keep the public statuses Confirmed, Qualified, and Intent, but require evidence provenance underneath them:

- Directly inspectable source/schema facts may be Confirmed at an exact SHA after an independent source check. “This enum has these cases” does not require CI.
- A behavioral claim supported only by the feature author's local run is Qualified as LocallyObserved, even when the command passed. The author report cannot be the sole basis for Confirmed.
- Confirmed behavioral claims require either an immutable CI result bound to the exact SHA or an independent actor's clean reproduction bound to the exact SHA, command, platform, configuration, exit status, and output digest.
- Performance, cross-platform, published-artifact, and deployed-site claims require evidence of that exact kind. Source presence or a narrower JVM test cannot substitute.
- CI is not magical authority: its workflow revision, dependencies, platforms, logs/artifacts, and failure-sensitive test must themselves be named. A green badge detached from the claimed SHA is no better than board prose.

Every material evidence record should name producer, relation to the change author, exact revision, command/court, environment/platform, outcome, artifact/log digest or durable locator, scope limits, reviewer, and the check showing the court can fail when the claim is false.

Practical effect now: the first site can publish source-checked architecture and API facts as Confirmed, local runtime observations as Qualified, and unfinished capabilities as Intent. The absence of CI limits the strength of behavioral claims; it need not delay authored orientation pages. Once CI exists, it may upgrade a claim only after producing the matching exact-SHA evidence—not merely because a workflow file exists.

This preserves the earlier rule that a test or receipt is necessary but not sufficient, and prevents “an agent said the tests passed” from being rendered as “the project independently verified this capability.”
